# Boomtect

> Boomtect is a browser app that simulates the sound of lightning, blasts, and sonic booms from their physics. A scene places sources (flashes, storms, blasts, barrages, fireworks, volcanic explosions, supersonic flights, meteors, whips, falling boosters) and microphones in 3D over real terrain and layered air, and renders what each microphone hears. It is a creative tool for sound design: a result is a plausible event, not a reconstruction or a measurement, and levels are uncalibrated model values in pascals.

Boomtect runs entirely in the browser, with no account and no server of its own. Every source is a set of points, each with a position, an emission time, and a pressure pulse; each pulse travels to each microphone with its own delay and loss, and the microphone hears their sum. Every part of the model is marked A (first principles), B (literature), or C (heuristic or synthetic).

Exports are 32-bit float WAV at one full scale in pascals, recorded in the scene JSON; per-microphone files start at the same moment. A scene is JSON with `"format": "boomtect.scene"` and opens again as a scene. A sound sent to Echotect is mono pressure without terrain echoes with a `tect.handoff` JSON: positions in metres east, north, and up from the place's geographic point, angles in compass degrees clockwise from north. A handoff reader fills in missing fields with defaults and never refuses an older or newer version.

Opened from each other, Boomtect and Rumbletect link their windows: they share the scene's place, terrain, air, ground, microphones, and render settings, each renders only its own emitters, and the microphones hear the sum, which the plots, levels, playback, and export use.

An agent can render without the browser: clone the repository and run `node tools/render.mjs <scene.json> <folder>` with Node 20 or later and no installed packages. A partial scene is enough; the folder gets one WAV per microphone and the filled scene, and stdout gives levels, length, and spectral shape so the result can be checked without listening. Start from the nearest file in `examples/` and change what the request names.

## Docs

- [README](https://github.com/janne-s/Boomtect/blob/main/README.md): what every control does, the export files, and the model table with sources and classes
- [Rendering from a script or an agent](https://github.com/janne-s/Boomtect/blob/main/README.md#rendering-from-a-script-or-an-agent): the render command, its output, and what each change does to the sound
- [Examples](https://github.com/janne-s/Boomtect/tree/main/examples): starting scenes for requests
- [Live app](https://janne-s.github.io/Boomtect/)

## Formats

- [Scene](https://github.com/janne-s/Boomtect/blob/main/src/domain/scene.js): every parameter with its default and range
- [Handoff](https://github.com/janne-s/Boomtect/blob/main/src/shared/domain/handoff.js): the `tect.handoff` format shared with Echotect and Rumbletect
- [Constants](https://github.com/janne-s/Boomtect/blob/main/src/domain/constants.js): the model's tuning values and limits

## Optional

- [Echotect](https://janne-s.github.io/Echotect/llms.txt): echoes from buildings, streets, and terrain for a sound, including one sent from Boomtect
- [Rumbletect](https://janne-s.github.io/Rumbletect/llms.txt): the continuous sound of jets, airliners, rockets, and volcanic eruptions, on the same terrain and air
